title: PROPOSED private AttemptCustodyV1 (ledger-owned monotone attempt phase and outcome)
standing: Design/reference proposal only: no acceptance, no readiness, no application and no implementation authorization. Private local operational record. Not a public request, wire schema, authority token or extension to any Run/receipt/journal schema.

siblingPrivateRecords.storeInstanceLineage: docs/v2/architecture/store-instance-lineage.v1.json (PS-01 owner; consumed unchanged, nothing redefined here)

normativeSelfContainment: This file states its own law. It requires no scratch/ path, no superseded draft and no reference model to be read for any operative rule. Citations to scratch/ or to earlier runtimes appear only as clearly labelled historical evidence.
revisionNote: Corrects the v6 bytes on four counts root identified. (1) phaseOutcomeCoupling carried a DUPLICATE admitted key, which a strict parser rejects and which a last-wins parser silently masked; the two blocks are merged into one. (2) tracedExistingOwners claimed the existing uniqueness reservation makes the admitted phase existing law and that no second record is added; both contradicted the corrected identity section 2 scoping and are replaced. (3) the phase description and the writer law named the cleanup path as a writer, which would license a write from a stopped session. (4) joins.toReceipt made runId, commitSequence and inventoryDigest conditional on caller-supplied fields; all three are now mandatory and come from admission, never from a caller.

tracedExistingOwners.standing: Traced before proposing anything. What existing law gives, and what it does NOT give, are stated separately.
tracedExistingOwners.whatExistingLawGives: Identity section 2 requires that both RequestId and ExecutionId use independent 16-byte host-CSPRNG draws, reserved with uniqueness checked in the corresponding operational ledger before use. That is a PRE-USE UNIQUENESS rule and it applies to every request mode.
tracedExistingOwners.whatExistingLawDoesNotGive: It does NOT establish durable permanent storage of an attempt record for all request modes, and it does NOT by itself establish the admitted phase. A uniqueness check before use can be satisfied without retaining a durable per-attempt row after the request ends. Treating the reservation sentence as proof of durable persistence was the v6 error and is withdrawn.
tracedExistingOwners.whatThisRecordAdds: A SEPARATE, SCOPED durable private record. It is scoped to durable-authoritative commit-capable attempts using the evidence ledger, meaning exactly those attempts that can publish an authoritative commit receipt through the guarded commit facade. It is an addition to existing law, not a restatement of it, and it does not weaken or restate the uniqueness rule.
tracedExistingOwners.excludedModes: Read-only requests and explicitly non-authoritative --ephemeral attempts acquire NO row here: no persistent evidence-ledger write and no security operation reference. Identity section 5 owns --ephemeral as non-authoritative, using temporary custody and minting no authoritative commit receipt, and that ownership is consumed unchanged.
tracedExistingOwners.executionIdCarriers: The commit receipt (identity section 5 step 3) and CommitRecoveryAssociationV1 both carry executionId. D9 fixes requiredTerminationIdentity as executionId and states that a settled ExecutionId is terminal for RETRY purposes.
tracedExistingOwners.operationRefCarriers: The journal carries operation_ref on every record type, and RCO, ICO, CLN and REV terminate an operation.
tracedExistingOwners.theActualGap: Nothing durably records that a PARTICULAR commit-capable ExecutionId reached a terminal state when it did NOT commit. The executionId-to-operationRef map is private host state whose only durable home is the association row, which exists only on success. Identity section 6 states that read-only recover(ExecutionId) inspects the committed receipt after a lost acknowledgement; it has no statement for the absent-receipt case.
alternativesConsideredAndRejected: A separately timed liveness probe after the ledger snapshot. Rejected: that is the race root's schedule 2 defeats.

A non-blocking LOCK_EX writer-lease census by the reader. Sound in principle, but the S7 census pattern requires the install fence and read-only recovery must not take the fence. It is instead what the authorized settlement sweep uses.
A caller-supplied settled D9 termination as the precondition. Works whenever a caller holds one, but cannot cover a crashed writer that never emitted a termination.

canonicalProfile.selected: product / foundation canonicalizer of identity-and-evidence section 3
canonicalProfile.rules: no normalization, integers to 2^64-1, H(domain, descriptor) where a domain digest is taken, raw SHA-256 over the exact canonical bytes where a plain digest is taken
canonicalProfile.why: Security section S2 splits the two profiles and states that a decoder for one never admits the other's documents. The metadata profile covers signed security metadata: root, catalog, revocation, JOURNAL RECORDS, recovery challenge and epoch, and platform profile population. This record is none of those. It is private storage/ledger operational metadata in the same family as CommitRecoveryAssociationV1, whose storeGenerationDigest is already a raw SHA-256 over canonical bytes.
canonicalProfile.contrastToStateExplicitly: The journal body_sha256 this record joins against IS domain-framed under opensip.metadata.journal.1. This record's own digests are NOT. Conflating the two is the exact error the earlier followup predicate made, so the two profiles are named at every join.

recordSchema.description: Constant 1; reject unknown versions before any join.

storeGenerationDigest.description: Raw SHA-256 of the canonical private store-generation binding, exactly the value the association uses. Its owner is docs/v2/architecture/store-instance-lineage.v1.json; this record consumes the binding tuple and digest shape unchanged and allocates nothing.

namespaceId.description: Exact registered project namespace; binary equality, no path resolution.

executionId.description: The reserved attempt ExecutionId of a durable-authoritative commit-capable attempt, product successor grammar, end-anchored.

operationRef.description: The security-owned operation token for this attempt, keeping its own grammar. This is the durable home of the executionId-to-operationRef correlation for attempts that never commit, which is why no member is added to the closed schema-3 JournalRecord to correlate a pending REV.

phase.description: Monotone, two-valued. admitted is written by the guarded commit facade when a durable-authoritative commit-capable attempt is admitted; it is NOT written for read-only or --ephemeral requests and is not a side effect of the generic uniqueness reservation. settled is written ONLY by an authorized writer that currently holds the custody its write requires: the guarded commit facade while its session is live, or the authorized settlement sweep under fence plus EXCLUSIVE. A stopped cleanup-only session may NOT write it. The only lawful transition is admitted to settled.

settledOutcome.description: Null exactly while phase is admitted. Exactly two settled outcomes, committed or refused, because those are the only two an observer can prove. There is deliberately NO undetermined outcome: see durabilityUndeterminedIsNotACustodyOutcome. Records what happened; it authorizes nothing.

durabilityUndeterminedIsNotACustodyOutco.finding: An earlier draft carried a third settled outcome, undetermined. That state is UNRESOLVABLE: the row is immutable once settled, so nothing could ever move a settled+undetermined attempt to a real outcome, and undetermined cannot prove absence without actual durable reconciliation. It is removed.
durabilityUndeterminedIsNotACustodyOutco.correctSeparation: durability-undetermined is a D9 RESPONSE to the caller at the time the commit syscall or barrier failed: operational-failed / DURABILITY.COMMIT_FAILED / durability-commit, with the ExecutionId retained, the runId omitted and no automatic retry. It is not a durable custody claim.
durabilityUndeterminedIsNotACustodyOutco.whatTheRowDoes: An attempt whose durability was uncertain stays phase=admitted, because its terminality is genuinely unknown at that moment. The authorized settlement sweep later resolves it to committed or refused from one coherent ledger snapshot under fence plus EXCLUSIVE custody.
durabilityUndeterminedIsNotACustodyOutco.twoSensesOfTerminal: D9 terminality of a settled ExecutionId means no retry of that attempt is ever admitted. It does NOT mean this record's phase is settled. An attempt can be D9-terminal to its caller while its custody row is still admitted, and the sweep is what closes that gap.

phaseOutcomeCoupling.admitted: settledOutcome is null and the attempt is not terminal in this record's sense, so no negative conclusion is available. If a joined receipt IS present this is the LAWFUL pre-settle interval, not a defect: the settle write is ordered after the receipt write, so every committing attempt passes through it. The receipt establishes historical commitment and pending settlement is disclosed operationally.
phaseOutcomeCoupling.settled+committed: A receipt and association for this exact primary key MUST exist in the same coherent ledger snapshot. If they do not, that is a contradiction between two rows the same transaction family owns: report the contradiction and unavailable history. NEVER terminal-not-committed.
phaseOutcomeCoupling.settled+refused: No receipt and no association exist for this primary key, and the writer that wrote this outcome held custody proving no other writer for this attempt could commit. This is the ONLY outcome that can support a negative conclusion, and only together with a confirmed absent receipt in the same snapshot.
phaseOutcomeCoupling.noThirdOutcome: There is no undetermined outcome. An attempt whose durability was uncertain stays admitted until the authorized sweep resolves it.

negativeConclusionRule.statement: terminal-not-committed requires ALL of: phase settled; settledOutcome exactly refused; no receipt row for the primary key; no association row for the primary key; all four observed in ONE coherent ledger snapshot.
forbidden: Concluding a negative from phase alone.
Concluding a negative from absence in an in-memory active set.
Concluding a negative from two separately timed observations.
Concluding a negative because this record is MISSING; see missingRowWithPresentReceipt.

missingRowWithPresentReceipt.case: A receipt and association are present and joined, this record is ABSENT for that primary key, and no legacy custody record exists either.
missingRowWithPresentReceipt.whyItHappens: Lawfully, for any attempt that committed before this record was selected, and for any store generation whose attempts predate it. It is not evidence of a defect.
missingRowWithPresentReceipt.selectedLaw: Report custody-unknown for the SETTLEMENT question while reporting the COMMITMENT question from the receipt and association, which remain valid historical evidence. The commitment answer is committed-historically; the settlement standing is custody-unknown-legacy.
missingRowWithPresentReceipt.forbidden: It is NEVER a negative, never terminal-not-committed, and never a licence to synthesize or forge a row of any kind. The absence of this record is silence about settlement, not a claim about commitment.

purgedReceiptLaw.statement: A historical receipt that was retained and later purged must NEVER become never-committed.
purgedReceiptLaw.logicalVersusPhysical: Two different observations must not be conflated. A LOGICAL retained record (sealed manifest, provenance, tombstone) that still names the Run means the receipt EXISTS as history even when its unshared evidence bytes have been reclaimed; that is committed with degraded availability. A raw both-absent observation means no receipt and no association row is present at all in this store generation.
purgedReceiptLaw.mechanism: Purge retains the minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone (identity section 5). So a purged committed attempt is never a raw both-absent observation: the tombstone or retained manifest is the logical evidence that distinguishes the two.
purgedReceiptLaw.noForgery: The distinction is made by READING the retained tombstone or manifest. No receipt is ever reconstructed, synthesized or forged from a tombstone, and a tombstone is never presented as a receipt.
purgedReceiptLaw.consequence: The negative conclusion rule additionally requires settledOutcome refused, which a purge can never produce, so no purge can flip a committed attempt to a negative even if its bytes are gone.

joins.correctionNote: An earlier draft said the receipt carries the store binding, and made three of its members conditional on caller-supplied fields. Both are corrected. The actual owner, docs/coop/design-corrections/foundation/identity-schemas.v3.json $defs/commit-receipt, is CLOSED with additionalProperties false and exactly eight members: schemaVersion, runId, executionId, namespaceId, commitSequence, inventoryDigest, sealedAssurance, signerKeyId. There is NO storeGenerationDigest on the receipt and none is implied. No member is widened.
joins.toReceipt: Where the caller supplies them, executionId and namespaceId join this record by binary equality. runId, commitSequence and inventoryDigest join the RECEIPT to the ASSOCIATION, and all three are required every time: they are taken from the admitted receipt bytes and the admitted association row, never from caller-supplied request fields, and a caller omitting them does not relax the join. commitSequence compares the receipt's exact integer against the association's canonical decimal text through the one private ordering accessor, never by lexical string compare. schemaVersion, sealedAssurance and signerKeyId are verified by the receipt's own admission and signer/custody checks, not by this join.
joins.toStoreBinding: The store binding is NOT joined through the receipt, because the receipt has no such member. It is established through the admitted store handle and registry, which yield the store-generation binding, and is carried by CommitRecoveryAssociationV1.storeGenerationDigest. This record's storeGenerationDigest must equal the association's; a mismatch is caught at that owning join, not inferred from the receipt.
joins.toAssociation: (storeGenerationDigest, namespaceId, executionId) is CommitRecoveryAssociationV1's primary key, so the association row is the same attempt by construction, and it is the only place the store binding and the receipt values meet.
joins.toOperation: operationRef equals the operationRef the association carries when an association exists, and is the sole durable correlation when it does not.
joins.toCarrier: this record carries NO carrier field. The carrier join is the association's journalCarrierDigest, grantGeneration, journalSeq and journalBodySha256, where journalBodySha256 is the DOMAIN-FRAMED journal body digest, not a raw SHA-256.
joins.whereABindingMismatchIsCaught: At the association join. A receipt naming the right namespaceId and executionId but sitting under a different store generation is detected because the association's storeGenerationDigest differs from the one the admitted handle produced, and the read-only conclusion is binding-unusable rather than a commitment claim.

laws: Written only by an authorized writer that currently holds the custody its write requires: the guarded commit facade while its session is live, or the authorized settlement sweep under the install fence plus EXCLUSIVE on the namespace. A stopped cleanup-only session may NOT write this record; it releases and leaves the row admitted for the sweep.
Low-level row insertion stays private; no INSERT OR REPLACE, mutation-on-read, unchecked restore constructor or convenience API may bypass these invariants.
admitted to settled is the only transition. Never reversed, never deleted, never re-opened, no second row for the same primary key, and settledOutcome is never rewritten once set.

The settle write is ordered AFTER the receipt write, so one coherent ledger snapshot can never show settled+committed without a receipt that was committed earlier, and a receipt present while the row is still admitted is lawful.

It authorizes nothing. Settling records an outcome and never licenses a retry, so the D9 law that a settled ExecutionId is terminal for retry purposes is preserved exactly. A later attempt after authority restoration receives a fresh ExecutionId.
Read by read-only recovery in the SAME snapshot as the receipt and the association, never through a second separately timed query.
Excluded from every semantic hash, Run identity, Coverage, Plan bound and public schema. It adds no field to the closed receipt or JournalRecord schemas.

Scoped to durable-authoritative commit-capable attempts. A read-only request or an --ephemeral attempt neither creates nor requires a row, and its absence for such a request is not a custody condition.
proposedPrivateDDL:
CREATE TABLE attempt_custody (
  store_generation_digest TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(store_generation_digest) = 64 AND store_generation_digest GLOB '[0-9a-f]*'),
  namespace_id    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(namespace_id) BETWEEN 1 AND 4096),
  execution_id    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (execution_id GLOB 'exec1_[0-9a-f]*' AND length(execution_id) = 38),
  operation_ref   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (operation_ref GLOB 'op-[0-9a-f]*' AND length(operation_ref) = 35),
  record_schema   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (record_schema = 1),
  phase           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (phase IN ('admitted','settled')),
  settled_outcome TEXT CHECK (settled_outcome IS NULL OR settled_outcome IN ('committed','refused')),
  CHECK ((phase = 'admitted' AND settled_outcome IS NULL)
      OR (phase = 'settled'  AND settled_outcome IS NOT NULL)),
  PRIMARY KEY (store_generation_digest, namespace_id, execution_id)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TRIGGER ac_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON attempt_custody
  BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'attempt custody is append-and-settle only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER ac_monotone BEFORE UPDATE ON attempt_custody
  BEGIN
    SELECT CASE WHEN OLD.phase = 'settled'
      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'attempt custody is already settled') END;
    SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.phase <> 'settled' OR NEW.settled_outcome IS NULL
      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'the only lawful transition is admitted to settled') END;
    SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.store_generation_digest <> OLD.store_generation_digest
              OR NEW.namespace_id <> OLD.namespace_id
              OR NEW.execution_id <> OLD.execution_id
              OR NEW.operation_ref <> OLD.operation_ref
              OR NEW.record_schema <> OLD.record_schema
      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'attempt custody identity is immutable') END;
  END;
ddlStanding: SELECTED placement: the storage-owned evidence ledger, within the already inventoried crates/storage/src/ledger_store.rs, commit.rs and recovery.rs modules. The authorized settlement sweep writes through that same ledger and the same table, so it needs no separate DDL. This is a settled selection.

readOnlyRecoveryUse.receiptPresentAndPhaseSettledCommitted: committed-historically; proceed to the carrier capture and anchor selection
readOnlyRecoveryUse.receiptPresentAndPhaseAdmitted: committed-historically with pendingSettlement disclosed; proceed to the carrier capture. LAWFUL interval, not a contradiction, and it revives no authority
readOnlyRecoveryUse.receiptPresentAndPhaseSettledRefused: contradiction: unknown-custody; preserve rows, synthesize nothing
readOnlyRecoveryUse.receiptPresentAndNoRow: committed-historically with custody-unknown-legacy for the settlement question; never a negative
readOnlyRecoveryUse.receiptAbsentAndPhaseSettledCommitted: contradiction: unknown-custody, unavailable history, never a negative
readOnlyRecoveryUse.receiptAbsentAndPhaseAdmitted: unknown-attempt-open. A durability-uncertain attempt lands here too; the authorized sweep resolves it

notEstablished: No OS durability, fsync behaviour or real crash behaviour for this row. That is product qualification, not an architectural gap.
The DDL was executed only against in-memory SQLite for its constraint and trigger behaviour; no on-disk ledger was created or migrated.
The authorized settlement sweep is specified and its decision matrix is reference-executed; its EXECUTION remains qualification.
